title: Confidently wrong intent (confidence >= 0.8)
hypothesis: Confidence is poorly calibrated: the model reports high certainty on examples it misreads, so the low-confidence escalation safety net never triggers for them.

examples.text: Just to inform everyone, I got the Spotify/Hulu student discount. So no one will probably see me these next few days.
examples.reply_draft: Hey there! Enjoy the tunes and the shows, fingers crossed you love it! 💚 /AI

examples.text: I need help! The app keeps creating new playlists labelled "tracks" with only one song in each one. How do I stop this?
examples.reply_draft: Hey there! Sorry to hear that. Could you let us know what device you're using and your Spotify app version? We'll take a look 🙂 /AI
Hey there! Thanks for sharing your feedback with us, we'll certainly pass this along. Let us know if you need a hand with anything else. /AI

proposed_fix: Calibrate confidence against dev accuracy (e.g. temperature scaling or a stricter rubric for reporting confidence) and route high-confidence disagreements with the rules to review.

title: Unnecessary escalation with reason 'low_confidence'
hypothesis: The 'low_confidence' trigger fires on benign mentions (e.g. a keyword used in a different sense), so self-serve cases are pushed to humans and the auto-handle rate suffers.

examples.text: I need help! The app keeps creating new playlists labelled "tracks" with only one song in each one. How do I stop this?
examples.reply_draft: Hey there! Sorry to hear that. Could you let us know what device you're using and your Spotify app version? We'll take a look 🙂 /AI
examples.why: agent escalated with low_confidence; gold says auto-handle

examples.text: for some reason, i cannot play any Beck songs on my desktop app. I have no problems playing anything else. "this song is not avail"
examples.reply_draft: Hey there! Sorry to hear that. Does logging out > restarting the device > logging back in help? Keep us posted /AI
examples.why: agent escalated with low_confidence; gold says auto-handle

examples.text: us independent Artists are having issues to log in and check our stats. Green button not working on log in page. Thanks
examples.reply_draft: Hey there! This is something for our Artist Services team. You can reach out to them via the help article for assistance with logging in. Let us know how it goes 🙂 /AI
examples.why: agent escalated with low_confidence; gold says auto-handle

proposed_fix: Narrow the 'low_confidence' trigger (negative look-arounds, require co-occurring intent) or let the LLM overrule it when the message is clearly self-serve.

title: Reply invents a link or policy (judge flag)
hypothesis: The draft reaches beyond retrieved evidence, inventing help links or promises the brand never made historically.

examples.text: I've got the "Get a year of Premium" offer splash screen on my iOs app, but there wasn't any CTA to apply just a button to open a webpage... and there is no button, link or anything... How can I appl…
examples.reply_draft: Hey there! Help's here. Can you try heading to this link:? Let us know how it goes 🧐 /AI
examples.why: The reply fails to provide a functional link, rendering it useless and hallucinating a solution that isn't there.

examples.text: if you really cared, you'd fix your Roku app. Not being able to access my playlists is really getting in the way of my Xmas spirit.
examples.reply_draft: Hey there! We have some info about the Spotify app on Roku here:. Give us a shout if there's anything else 🙂 /AI
examples.why: The reply is broken because it references a help article link that is missing from the message.

examples.text: song sharing on Android crashes the app every time. Known issue yet?
examples.reply_draft: Hey there! Our developers are looking into this, and we'll keep everyone updated. Let us know how it goes 🙂 /AI
examples.why: This reply makes an unverified claim that developers are looking into the issue without gathering necessary diagnostic information.

proposed_fix: Constrain replies to links present in the evidence (post-generation link whitelist) and instruct the model to ask for a DM instead of stating policy.

title: Gold intent 'other' predicted as 'feature_request_or_feedback'
hypothesis: Messages about other share surface vocabulary with feature_request_or_feedback; the model latches onto the more frequent reading instead of the customer's actual ask.

examples.reply_draft: Hey there! Thanks for sharing your feedback with us, we'll certainly pass this along. Let us know if you need a hand with anything else. /AI

examples.text: Your new app looks great on iPhone x! Thanks for the update!
examples.reply_draft: Hey there! Thanks for the kind words – we appreciate it. Enjoy the update! /AI

examples.text: . Any ETA on solving this issue?: <url>
examples.reply_draft: Hey! We're afraid we don't have any info to share, but rest assured we’re working on it as we speak. Stay tuned 🙂 /AI

proposed_fix: Add contrastive examples of 'other' vs 'feature_request_or_feedback' to the taxonomy description and sharpen the boundary rule in the classification prompt.
